Any Meningitis symptoms the earlier you are seen the better the outcome will be. My symptoms:- fever, severe headache which I thought was a migraine, photophobia & sensitive to sound, stiff neck, nausea & vomiting & feeling really run down. Due to being clinically vulnerable I’ve had to have IV antivirals. I count myself VERY lucky that it isn’t bacterial Meningitis. ⚠️ Sharing this for awareness. ⚠️💖 #meningitis #viralmeningitis #viralmeningitisawareness #meningitisawareness #meningitisstory #awareness #sharingforawareness

Meningitis affects more than 5m people globally each year 1/10 die as a result 2/10 left with an impairment like brain injury or amputation As a survivor of bacterial meningitis. The symptoms could be mistaken for flu.  Symptoms are a high temperature cold hands and feet vomiting confusion breathing quickly muscle and joint pain pale, mottled or blotchy skin spots or a rash headache a stiff neck a dislike of bright lights being very sleepy or difficult to wake fits (seizures) Babies may also: refuse feeds be irritable have a high-pitched cry have a stiff body or be floppy or unresponsive have a bulging soft spot on the top of their head Someone with meningitis, septicaemia or meningococcal disease can get a lot worse very quickly. Once the antibiotics kick in and you are feeling a little better some ppl experience the after effects Memory loss/lack of concentration/difficulty retaining information Clumsiness/co-ordination problems Headaches Deafness/hearing problems/tinnitus/dizziness/loss of balance Epilepsy/seizures Weakness/paralysis/spasms Speech problems Loss of sight/vision problems After effects caused by sepsis Memory loss/lack of concentration/difficulty retaining information Clumsiness/co-ordination problems Arthritis/joint stiffness Scarring/skin damage Amputations Kidney damage Lung damage I Now suffer from quiet a few of these. #meningitis #recovery #meningitisawareness #meningitissurvivor

SRMA, relapse 🐶…..Here we go again 😢 All that effort for a nub of sausage stuffed in a bone as he’s had his food allowance 💔 Having a dog on steroids for SRMA is like having a dog that’s became a zombie dog after an apocalypse Still cute by really aggy , they are constantly hungry , they never sleep , when they do sleep they wake for the slightest sound of a packet of food or even a dish cloth being opened when once before they didn’t flinch , they want to drink constantly (water not blood) then need to wee like they didn’t wee 20 mins before , they walk around aimlessly, mostly in circles, are forever restless and just look at you dead dead behind the eyes waiting and grunting for something , you truly hope it’s for a cuddle but is food, it’s always FOOD! The list is endless of negatives to the treatment and we’re only on day 6 , but we’ve done it before , we shall do it again ……round two post the initial diagnosis which is utterly shit but it was bound to happen , it was statistically written in the stars ⭐️  6 months of this and counting …..roll on normality and having a healthy pup again……Fu*k SRMA🖕🏼 #srma #poorlypup #hungrypuppy #insicknessandinhealth #beagle #beagleofinstagram #beaglepuppy #srmasurvivor #srmasupporters #beaglelove #meningitis  Ps this isn’t a moan it’s just a frustration for us both , but we are where we are and the community on here was amazing first time round , so please only send love and happiness , negativity is not welcome 🤎  Equally all suggestions are welcome how to keep him feeling full or entertained 🦴

Hey everyone, does anyone else out there have their seizures triggered my singing, mine causes me to have temporal lobe seizures, it super rare :( is there anyone out there that has the same problem??  #antigadenchepalitis #encephalitis #encephalitisawareness #epilepsyawareness #epilepsy

Anyone out there???? Im going to see if the power of tik tok can help me find someone who may have the same health condition as me? I have anti gad encephalitis…. Encephalitis is inflammation of the brain, usually caused by an infection, it has caused me to have temporal lobe seizures :(  Anti-GAD enchepalitis is a a rare cause of autoimmune encephalitis that lacks symptom specificity, often leading to a failure in diagnosing or mischaracterizing the underlying etiology. Even singing triggers my seizures, which is RARE AGAIN….i have ivig infusions and on 2 types of epilepsy tablets, steroids and other supplements like calcium, vitamin d and zinc, i’ve started loosing my hair and started getting arthritis in my hands.. I have the most incredible husband who has supported me through all the scary phone calls were i’ve had a seizure and i’ve completely forgotten my memory, holds me when i cry when my hair is falling out and i’ve had a bad day, watches me have seizures and holds my hand. i have family that picks me up from my infusions, messages me all the time checking in. My work colleagues are so amazing, i have alot of them at work, hugging me helping me through the tough days, i know i have the most incredible support there and im so lucky. actually with my diagnoses i feel alone, there is no one on my ward when i have treatments with what i have, not a single soul, If there is anyone out there that is at all like me please please please reach out i really don’t want to feel so alone in this diagnoses anymore :(  In a way i hope i don’t find anyone because this has changed my life forever because its incurable but if there is someone out there we can support each other ♥️ Thankyou in advance tiktok x #encephalitis #support #pleaseshelp #antigadencephalitis #helpme #epilepsy #temporallobeseizures #seizures #seizureawareness #autoimmunedisease #brain #temporallobeepilepsy #temporallobeseizure

Dog meningitis is serious and can be fatal. Most types of dog meningitis can be treated successfully if caught early.  Here are some of the signs and symptoms to look out for:  Sleepier/ more lethargic than normal Muscle and joint aches and pains. Neck stiffness- with Jasper he was more withdrawn. He didn’t want cuddles and refused to jump up in the sofa. High temperature. Hot to touch or panting Refusal to eat or reduced appetite High infection markers on a blood test Loss of use of limbs You may not see all of these symptoms but if you notice some it is always worth suggesting dog meningitis to your vet. They may not have thought of it. With Jasper he was more withdrawn, his appetite had reduced, his poos were chalky, he didn’t want to jump up on the sofa, he didn’t want cuddles and he was not himself. We took him to the vets and they did a blood test. His infection markers were high. The vet told us it could just be an infection and to wait and see if he improves… we took him back to the vet several times in 3 weeks and at no point did they mention meningitis.  Towards the end of 3 weeks, Jasper started to lose the use of his legs. At this point the local vet thought he might have a prolapsed disc and referred him to the specialist hospital. They did an MRI and diagnosed meningitis (steroid responsive meningitis). At this point Jaspers inflammatory markers were in the 1,000s and they should have been under 5. We knew it was going to be an uphill battle but it was one Jasper fought valiantly.  Who knows if things would be different if our local vet had thought of meningitis earlier.  Follow your gut. You know your dog best. If you think something is wrong be insistent. Suggest meningitis if you notice any of these signs or symptoms.  #dogmeningitis #dog #dogmeningitisawareness #dogs #dogsofinstagram #dogsonwheels #dogsofsomerset #dogstagram #dogsofinstaworld #cavapoo #cavapooworld #cavapoopuppy #braveboy #fight #meningitis #cavoodle #cavoodles #cavoodlesofinstagram #cavoodlepuppy #cavoodlegram #cavoodlelove #dogstory #dogshavelivestoo #mypuppystory #savingpuppy #morethanjustadog #dogloveofmylife #fortheloveofdogs

10 days ago our life fell apart when our Jax fell ill with meningitis-encephalitis (meningoencephalitis)  Jax was placed in an induced coma and rushed to @Alder Hey’s intensive care unit. I will forever be grateful to this amazing hospital for looking after Jax and getting him back to a stable condition 🫶🏽❤️ He would not be here today if it was not for them.  Today just 3 days later jax has managed to throw a ball on his own and is starting to have more sensations in his arms, hands and legs!  He has a long road to recovery ahead of him but every day hes suprising us more and more 💫   I cannot stress enough if you are not happy with a Dr’s first opinion, PLEASE get another dr’s opinion. Jaxon was send home with a (viral) from A+E at our local hospital despite me asking for bloods to be done and explain his drowsiness and light sensitivity. Just because your child doesnt have a rash doesnt mean its not meningitis or encephalitis! Or in jax’s case both! Im lucky to be abke to cuddle by boy due not being listened to so if i can help prevent this happening again, I will! Do not take no for an answer!  Hes in the best hospital now for rehabilitation and to get him back on his feet 👏🏽👏🏽 I couldnt be prouder of how strong he is! All at 4 years old. ❤️💔  #meningitis #meningitisawareness #encephalitis #enchepalitiswarior #awareness #alderheychildrenshospital #poorlybaby #recovery #rehab #miracle #fighter #champ #futurerugbystars

Today is #PANDAS #panspandasawarenessday  It's been 9 years since Layla got #PANDAS and only 9 months since diagnosis. In that time the longest she has gone #seizure and #ticattack free is 18 solid days. We were on Day 19 today. PANDAS known as Peadiatric Autoimmune Neuropsychiatric Disorder associated with Streptococcal #pandas is #debilitating and onset is 'sudden', over days, weeks, months. That doesn't mean every #symptom stays or appears at the same time. But within months Layla had EVERY symptom listed here! Each one blamed on a diagnosis of #crps or 'one of those things' or a child who 'wants attention'. Looking back can be soke destroying some days. But with #awareness comes #education and with this comes development in #treatment and hopefully less Layla's being not believed. It's also important to note Layla's #ehlersdanlos and comorbities were also 'missed' or delayed. With a #immunemediated  behaviour changes and #mcas we continue to learn as things just 'make sense' 9 years later. Did you know…?   - Meningitis can affect anyone of any age - Meningitis can kill - Meningitis can cause long-term after-effects - Viral and bacterial are the most common causes of meningitis - No vaccine provides 100% protection against meningitis - Early signs and symptoms can appear similar to ‘flu’ or a stomach bug   #Babies and young children are particularly vulnerable to #meningitis as they cannot easily fight infection because their immune system is not yet fully developed.   Symptoms in babies and toddlers include:   - Fever with cold hands and feet - Refusing food - Vomiting - Fretful, disliking being handled - Drowsy, floppy and unresponsive - Rapid breathing/grunting - Pale blotchy skin/rash that doesn’t fade - Unusual crying/moaning - Bulging fontanelle - Stiff neck - Dislike of bright lights - Having a seizure   Some bacteria that cause meningitis can also cause septicaemia (blood poisoning). The rash associated with meningitis is actually caused by septicaemia.   You should NEVER WAIT FOR A RASH, it can be a late sign or may not appear at all.   Always trust your instincts and get your child seen by a medical professional if you are worried about them. Meningitis reel   Did you know…?   - Meningitis can affect anyone of any age - Meningitis can kill - Meningitis can cause long-term after-effects - Viral and bacterial are the most common causes of meningitis - No vaccine provides 100% protection against meningitis - Early signs and symptoms can appear similar to 'flu' or a stomach bug   Babies and young children are particularly vulnerable to meningitis as they cannot easily fight infection because their immune system is not yet fully developed.   Symptoms in babies and toddlers include:   - Fever with cold hands and feet - Refusing food - Vomiting - Fretful, disliking being handled - Drowsy, floppy and unresponsive - Rapid breathing/grunting - Pale blotchy skin/rash that doesn’t fade - Unusual crying/moaning - Bulging fontanelle - Stiff neck - Dislike of bright lights - Having a seizure   Some bacteria that cause meningitis can also cause septicaemia (blood poisoning). The rash associated with meningitis is actually caused by septicaemia.   You should NEVER WAIT FOR A RASH, it can be a late sign or may not appear at all.   Always trust your instincts and get your child seen by a medical professional if you are worried about them. She complained of many #symptoms pain being the one obvious one. Then #tonsillitis then changes in feelings across her body, tummy ache, headaches, feeling 'ill'. We were referred for a scan, something I had to fight for as Layla's attendance dropped, school work suffered, her mood and fun, outgoing active personality disappeared. She was diagnosed in March with #crps met what we now know is the criteria for #ehlersdanlos HOWEVER every symptom for #pandas #encephalitis was met in the 12 months following her first #strepinfection AS SOON as someone mentioned it may be #complexregionalpainsyndrome EVERYOTHER symptom was dismissed. Speak up, ask for help if you feel you aren't being heard. As we approach our baby girls 18th Birthday, I'm reminded of that first big relapse, the one we were told was 'the excitement of xmas'. What a crock of 💩 💩 💩.  It was #strep more than likely. 1 #diagnosis does not mean you can't have another. BUT also that some hospitals do NOT care. BEFORE commenting 'call an ambulance', or 'why you moving the camera?'. It is explained in this video BUT again the camera shows me and her doctor or any paramedic (if needed) the context and changes. It ALSO gives me the time of seizures and the gaps in between. last January layla was taking my ambulance to #uhcw because during seizures her oxygen was dropping significantly to warrant it. I was asked on yesterday's video, 'but wouldn't discharging her affect your care next time?' This was last year and another reason why Layla refuses to go! I put in a complaint in August 2022 about being discharged with NO referrals for ekg and #neurologist as per guidelines. THIS DID NOT HAPPEN. The hospital #complaints team is 'too short staffed and busy' to reply to this complaint. Since presenting and advising we have an #encephalitis diagnosis we still get the same.  I hope this makes at least 1 person understand a little better. THE #gaslighting from the top and its consultants is the issue! Its a teaching hospital sk unfortunately those learning are just learning the how not to care for people way and or becoming mentally burnt out in the process. This hospital when it comes to Laylas #crps and symptoms linked to #pandas and #mcas and #ehlersdanlos have been a joke. They are putting people lives at risk and its not as easy as 'choose another hospital' or ask to go elsewhere. Even now I've spent over £5000 to get answers we still don't have support. 9 years! when will this end? #fyp #viral #PANDAS #panspandas #BGE #basalganglia #encephalitis #autoimmunedisease #mcas #mastcellactivationsyndrome #gaslighting #uhcw #complaint #AE #accidentandemergency #PALS

HOW TO SPOT SEPSIS IN BABIES AND CHILDREN CHILDREN   A child may have sepsis if he or she: - Is breathing very fast - Has a ‘fit’ or convulsion - Looks mottled, bluish, or pale - Has a rash that does not fade when you press it - Is very lethargic or difficult to wake - Feels abnormally cold to touch   If you spot any of these signs, call 999 or go straight to A&E and Just ask: “could it be sepsis?”   A child under 5 may have sepsis if he or she: - Is not feeding - Is vomiting repeatedly - Has not passed urine for 12 hours   If you spot any of these signs, call 111 or see your GP and Just ask: “could it be sepsis?”   Please SHARE this to help raise awareness in parents.  #daisyfirstaid #babyfirstaid #meningitis #sepsis #firstaid

Health disparities between genders have long been a topic of interest in healthcare discussions. The reality however is of a deep-rooted and multifaceted gender inequality which exists world-wide. Research shows: • More women than men say they have a health problem in 2024  • At present, two-fifths (40%) of women in the UK say they’re currently experiencing a condition related to their health  • Whilst 35% of men say the same. (forthwithlife 2024) Improving fairness and tackling inequalities and disparities and more research into the health needs of women is needed in my opinion, despite this 'apparently being a priority' in the UK. So many of us are told 'It's womens problems', or 'you're a young girl, it's growing pains or anxiety'. So add in other oppressive inequalities and others marginalised due to their gender we need to keep #advocating and speaking up.  *I recognise that me & Layla hold   certain privileges. #GoFundMe #raisingmoney #braininjury #encephalitis #rehabilitation #fyi #fyp  Hi, my name is Ching and raising funds for John Phillip known as “Phil” for his private rehabilitation.  At 05 May 2024. A date that John Philipp Uriarte known as Phil, his partner Joyce and his families will not forget. On May 4, 2023, he arrived in Inverness complaining about a headache, when I arrived from the Isle of Skye to see him that day I called an ambulance midday but they didn’t take him to the hospital after checking up on him and told us to continue giving him paracetamol at that same night, I woke up to the noise of Phil chewing something, doing some unusual stuff, unaware of what he was doing, I immediately called the ambulance again this time he was assisted right away and blue-lighted to Raigmore Hospital and straight to ITU. Phil’s life changed after a severe headache and was diagnosed with necrotising encephalitis. As most of you are aware Phil was in hospital for almost 8 months (35 days in ITU and remaining days in the ward), his life changed in an instant.  Now, after nearly a year Phil needs your help as he continues his rehab journey. I have hands down, that he is been looked after by our community GP, nurses, physio, OT and speech and language therapy, but he requires extra rehabilitation (intense rehab to improve his quality of life) which we don’t have enough facilities in our community to give continuation in his treatment. I am worried he will lose full mobility and speech in it and it’s about time and need to try different things not covered by NHS.  For all you know Phil, he used to work in Dunollie Hotel as a General Assistant and in COOP as a retail assistant and has lived in Broadford for about 7 years now. He was loved by many, a gamer, a longboarder and a driver to everyone. His fit and healthy until last May 2023 a day after he arrived from the Philippines to take his fiancee Joyce to have their wedding supposed to be last June 2023 and settled down here in the UK afterwards but life doesn’t always turn out the way we expect and wanted. The last 10 months have been incredibly challenging for Phil and Joyce ( as we are still processing her visa to remain here in the UK so she can be with Phil in these dark times), but his families, Phil and Joyce have always felt encouraged and supported by the outpouring of love and support from family, friends and community. Friends who become family.  During Phil’s months in therapy with physios, OTs and salt we saw many little triumphs but he still needs a lot of help and support for daily personal needs and activities. His recovery thus far has already but despite acknowledging how far he has come, he still feels a long way from the man that he was. Unfortunately, his speech, cognition, and mobility are significantly impacted due to his diagnosis; this will affect Phil’s ability to partake in the things that he wants to do. He is young, he will be turning 27 years old this month (April). He needs full assistance getting in/out of bed standing and walking, personal care, and feeding himself and his speech is not that clear yet. We all want Phil to be independent and have a better quality of life.  To facilitate that progress and keep hope alive, Phil needs help to access specialist neuro rehab. I did some research to find the right people to support Phil for the best possible outcomes, but their services come at a price.  This GoFundMe donation enables you to contribute the following: * £85 per hour = intense rehab at MOTIONrehab for a month/months  * £125 per hour = speech and language therapy * £2000-2,500 per month for accommodation while he is away for rehab Any amount you can give, however small can make a difference. Please donate what you can and share his story.  This is going to be the most intense part of Phil's rehabilitation journey but he is determined to get better and keep pushing him forward https://gofund.me/e187870f

How did your week go #rishisunak  Mine as a 40 year old #carer to my 18 year old (disabled myself) went like this... MONDAY- got Layla up, medication, supervised to the bathroom, dressed and then walked her trainee assistance dog (an auxiliary aid that is learning to alert to seizures, BECAUSE the #NHS after 2 years of seizures still refuse to recognise, treat and refer for testing), then I got them both to school. Cried some more, went into #autistic meltdown - took her for a hospital 🏥 appointment  THURSDAY- she woke after I'd got her up to do medication 💊 (like every morning), went into #seizures her legs didn't work, so I used the rollator which was DONATED because the NHS and local government have NOT in 9 years supported with housing adaptions. I cried some more, broke down, unable to do the basic tasks like feed myself and verbalise my needs. In a weeks time approx Layla sits her A-Levels, at home. Moving to 6th Form to the School she finally chose, has been the BEST decision. Her health declined further after this. But her new school put everything and more in place from day one.  Layla sits her exams all 7 I think at home with an #invigilator giving her the best possible chance. If she has a medical episode during then other contingencies are in the plan.  Her previous school had 4 years! I get angry at how someone's else, someone with a power imbalance, judging my parenting got to control her choices and use his ableist views to form the foundations of 'treatment'. It's led to #medicaltrauma and exacerbated problems, such as #painfulbladdersyndrome and #overactivebladderproblems now needing treatment after being dismissed for years. AND not to mention the #pain that's been uncontrolled, #dislocations and deterioration when #orthotics and #mobilityaids earlier could have supported. If your child has a new rash, apply a glass cup and apply gentle pressure on the affected skin area. If the rash disappears with pressure it is considered a 'blanching rash'. If the rash does not disappear, it is considered a 'non-blanching rash. There are multiple causes for a non blanching rash, but the most serious cause is meningitis. The type of rash, as well as other features such as temperature of your child, if they are drowsy or not can help decide how urgently they need to be seen. If you are worried about your child, always seek urgent medical advice. #skinrash #meningitis #newmum #mumsoftiktok #newdad #dadsoftiktok

With July being Disability Pride Month it makes it even more special that today marks ONE whole year since the handover of Layla's #wheelchair and  power assist wheels. When I say (as her Mum) I couldn't be PROUDER it is an understatement.  Around 14.1 million people in the UK are considered disabled. Yet, it wasn't until 1995 that legislation was passed, in order to protect the disabled community from discrimination. With that Law not being updated/replaced till The Equality Act 2010. Since Layla's health declined/changed, we have seen so much ableism, some of which we had to challenge ourselves over. But with the medical 'professionals' still using a 'one size fits all', 'if we can't see it, isn't real' along with an old school Medical Model, society often seems to be going backwards. Self #advocacy is something Layla has started to excel in, and having her wheelchair, has meant reserving energy, reduced dislocations and added pressure on her body that has led to her attending and more importantly taking part in SO much in one year. I am in awe of the strength she has. I am just so very sorry that you have had to go through what you have...BUT we have fought, often, well mainly when we shouldn't have had to.  Just use the mobility aid! Do what gives your body a rest! Speak up and if you feel you can't, just keep trying. Being disabled is not a dirty word. Just because you accept society and your illness disables you, does not make you less. Ofcourse you grieve your healthy body or the life you thought you'd have, it doesn't mean you've given up. It also doesn't mean everyday has to or is the same. Using a mobility aid suited to YOU can GIVE you life! #disabilityadvocate #disabilitypride #invisibleillness #chronicillness #wheelchair #ambulatorywheelchairuser #ambulatorywheelchairusersexist #mobilityaids #smartcrutches #ehlersdanlos #mcas #PoTs #crps #chronicpain #encephalitis #seizures

PANDAS/PANS affects the basal ganglia that operates movement. Tremors, Dystonia and the sense of her legs not connecting to her brain is something Layla has and still stuggles with. From 9 years old Layla-Jaye went from a normal active kid, into sports, always excelling at school with no major challenges, to almost over night being in #pain and more than 20 un answered #illness symptoms. Very quickly (less than 6 months) she was diagnosed with #CRPS #complexregionalpainsyndrome a REAL pain condition BUT so many other symptoms didn't 'fit'. When I say WE were told not to 'give in' to Layla and despite having a diagnosis of a syndrome described as the 'unaliving disease' she was told IF SHE WANTED to join in life, like school and day trips and exercise she WOULD! The 'excitement of Xmas' put her in a #wheelchair we NOW know Layla had #ehlersdanlos all along - missed for 8 years! Coeliac - missed for first 2 years! PANDAS - missed and now have an incorrect diagnosis of #FND on notes. Along with this comorbities of #mcas #pots and ##intestinaldysmotility and #painfulbladder . 🧠 Brudzinski’s & Kernig’s sign is conducted to evaluate suspected meningitis. 🤒 Brudzinski’s -Occurs as a result of meningeal inflammation -Head flexion causes meningeal irritation by movement of the spinal cord within the meninges  -The patient flex’s their hip to cancel out traction forces, lessening the irritation 🦵Kernig’s -Occurs as a result of meningeal inflammation due to movement of the spinal cord nerves against the meninges. -Extending the patients leg stretches the hamstring -Pulling on surrounding tissue near the spinal canal & meninges  -Resulting in the leg being unable to fully extend without pain or resistance  ⚠️ Both can raise suspicion towards meningitis however they are NOT a diagnostic tool to both rule in & out meningitis. Further testing is required in hospital. . 📷neurosurgicalfocus . 🚑 Hit follow & like for more prehospital content  . . #meningitis #pediatrics #medicaleducation

SU*CIDE. lets talk about it🖤  TW❗️ because the more we talk, the more lives could be saved. please, if it ever crosses your mind, talk to someone.  people are out there who can help. my suic*dal thoughts began very suddenly when i was 15, a year or so after my onset of PANS, encephalitis. it took years to find out my suicidal thoughts & planning wasn’t mental illness, it was brain inflammation. it was extremely scary and all finally came out when my teacher found me hiding in the library instead of being in maths.  after that, they crept back in all the time. like a black virus spreading across my brain begging for my attention. years ago, it was all teenage Evie thought about. now, i can’t think of anything worse. death scares me so much. brain inflammation still occasionally puts those thoughts into my head, but i know it’s not me.  did you know Lyme Disease has a very high suicide rate?💔 something else i’m diagnosed with and has also contributed. please stay❤️ its a permanent solution to a temporary problem. it really really can get better, the world wont feel dark forever 🫶🏻 Samaritans: 116 123 📞 #encephalitis #suicideprevention #mentalhealth #lymedisease #mentalhealthmatters #suicidepreventionday #braininflammation #PANS

For over a century, Sub-Saharan Africa’s meningitis belt endured devastating epidemics. Until 2010, when a breakthrough changed everything. 💉✨   With the introduction of the MenAfriVac, Group A meningitis cases were eliminated in the meningitis belt, saving countless lives and preventing unimaginable suffering. Now, with new immunisations targeting additional strains, Africa is on track to achieve something remarkable: the complete elimination of meningitis across the continent. 🌍💪   To keep this life-saving work going, we’re calling on world governments to support Gavi’s replenishment to protect 500 million children against diseases like meningitis between 2026-2030—preventing more than 8 million deaths and building global health security for the future.   #ForOurFuture #WorldMeningitisDay #meningitisawareness #meningitis #globalhealth #publichealth

⚠️Tics (swearing)⚠️ Did you know that #tics can be caused by multiple different reasons? They also can be a 'by product' of a condition, not a condition itself 🤔 Pandas is considered a #diagnosis when a SUDDEN onset of Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), tic disorder, or both suddenly appear following a streptococcal (strep) infection, such as strep throat or scarlet fever. It is thought that it is the #autoimmune response to #strep on the 🧠 causing an immune response (Source:NIMH,2024 and @PansPandasUK).  #PansPandasAwarenessDay #encephalitis #autoimmuneencephalitis #basalgangliainflammation #basalgangliaencephalitis #autoimmunedisease #tics #ticattack #ticawareness #ticdisorder #education #awareness #advocate

Challenges of 2025 🏃🏼‍♂️🚴🏼‍♂️🏊🏼‍♂️ We are wanting to raise a substantial amount of awareness and funds for @The Walton Centre Charity so that would only mean committing to something substantial!! 1️⃣ on the 12th of April 2025 I face my first challenge, @Santa Eulària Ibiza Marathon  26.2 miles in beautiful Balearic sunshine, Ibiza holds a very special place in our hearts and somewhere we continue to visit each year 2️⃣ June 2025 I will cycle a total of 3,200 miles from our home town in North Wales to The Walton Centre and back over 24 consecutive days. A brief note on how I came up with this number. In the UK 19,000 people are diagnosed each year with brain tumours, 5% of these are Meningiomas which Nik had, which is roughly 3,200 3️⃣ I will finish the year in Tenby and with the ultimate challenge of an @IRONMAN  Which will combine all my previous challenges plus a swim for good measure! 🏊🏼‍♂️2.4 mile swim 🚴🏼‍♂️112 mile cycle 🏃🏼‍♂️26.2 mile run We have a few other fundraising ideas in the pipeline but awaiting confirmation on these so stay tuned, this is not the end of our journey but the very beginning! #Disclaimer!! I haven't got on a bike in years! I've never ran a marathon and swimming is not my strong point 😮😳🤣 So for now I train and train hard under the watchful eyes of my PT and friend @well.fit.gym Mike was the person who I turned to after back surgery in 2021 and is a filing cabinet of knowledge, I wouldn't be attempting this without him  So stay tuned for this journey we will be documenting every step of the way, hopefully raise more awareness of brain tumours and some much needed funds to an amazing charity! ABOUT YESTERDAY 🤠🥳 The Live In The Living Room Gives Back event for @Meningitis Now at The Bedford was so amazing yesterday! 🤩 Despite the challenges that were faced in the lead up to the event (I, (James) thought about cancelling the event more than once 😢) it was so great to make the show a reality ❤️ Now for the thank you’s. This will probably sound like an Oscar’s speech lol. 🤣 Firstly, thank you to all 24 acts that played including ⬇️ 🎶 @Nick Edwards  🎶 @alanfinlanmusic  🎶 @Laketown  🎶 @"Mr" Paul Adams  🎶 @Robyn Red  🎶 @Tennessee Twin  🎶 @Chasing_Twisters  🎶 @Sanderson Scully  🎶 @Tony Bowen  🎶 @Amy Moore  🎶 Sophie Rose  🎶 Nicole Allen 🎶 AKA Chris and Tony 🎶 @SammieSoravia  🎶 @Sam Butler  🎶 @Jackson Lake Music  🎶 James Berryman  🎶 @isobelthatcher  🎶 @Andy Hewitt  🎶 The Old Mule  🎶 @Luke Edney  🎶 Ben Parkhurst  🎶 Rob Lewis  🎶 @FinPearson  Some of the performances were simply astounding! 🤩 Thank you to Dom from @Country Chat with Dom and Linda from @linda1.conway for being great hosts as per usual ❤️ Thank you to Dom, Linda and @dcbrownlive for hosting some great rounds ❤️ Thank you to The Bedford for always being an amazing venue to work with ❤️ Thank you to Rich and the other sound guy (who’s name I didn’t get unfortunately) for the amazing sound ❤️ Thank you to @Hayley for being an amazing Production Assistant ❤️ Thank you to everyone that came to the show and who donated money ❤️  This event was very important to me (James) as I almost died of Meningitis B when I was 18. The love and the support in the room was truly mind-blowing ❤️ On behalf of myself and anyone else affected by Meningitis, THANK YOU! ❤️❤️❤️  The final fundraising total will be announced very soon. Recently my daughter was in hospital with bacterial meningitis, this is why I have not been posting! I wanted to use my page to raise Awareness of bacterial meningitis- when i say meningitis doesnt mess about it doesnt, it all happened so fast! As soon as i saw the rash we went to a&e.  ‼️Trigger warning, images and details of an induced coma.‼️ On the 19/10/24 Sian went from eating a chinese without any symptoms of being unwell to within half an hour vomiting and diarrhoea.  Within 24 hours she was in an induced Coma.  Im not sure on time stamps on 20/10/24 but I know by the sunday evening my beautiful healthy daughter was put in an induced coma so her body had the chance of fighting and as a family we were told to say our goodbyes incase she didnt make it.  Due to my quick thinking, the Drs, Nurses and consultants I was lucky enough to bring my daughter home 2 weeks later.  Please look out for these symptoms, these are what sian had in order but symptoms may differ from person to person and age At Home: Vomiting and diarrhoea saturday evening Aching legs and Headache from what she discribed as all over the head Rash that did not disappear under a glass and was smooth to touch looked very similar to chicken pox at first some are blotted, some looked like blisters and by the time we got to the hospital dark purple/ blue ones appeared. - rash appeared quickly! (May not appear at all)  Symptoms that appeared in a&e  Stiff neck Light sensitivity  Delirium Awake but not responding I cant thank @norfolkandnorwichhospital enough for what they done! Absolute angels on earth! Thanks to the Nurses, Drs, consultants I got to bring my Daughter home! Within one week of being discharged she passed her driving test that we were going to cancel!! #bacterialmeningitis #icu #nurse #dr #consultant #raiseawareness #meningitis #inducedcoma

Lettie developed this rash 3 days ago. It started around her mouth and then started spreading to her arms and legs.  The first thing I did was grab a clear glass and press it against the rash. I was looking to see if the rash faded as I pressed the glass against it. Because the glass is clear it allowed me to see that the red spots disappear with pressure or better described as a ‘blanching rash.’  I didn’t just check this rash on day 1, I checked it every day. That’s because rashes can change and can sometimes become ‘non-blanching’ which means the spots or rash do NOT fade under pressure- this is a medical emergency  Why? A rash that does not disappear with the glass test could potentially be a sign of sepsis caused by meningitis. Babies and young children can deteriorate quickly with meningitis. The key here is to seek help urgently.  Don’t base your decision to seek help based on the glass test results alone. Even if your child’s rash disappears with the glass test but they look unwell and you’re worried, you must still seek help and trust your instincts.  Top tip for darker skin where this test might be harder to decipher- try areas such as the palms of hands or soles of feet or the tummy and make sure you’ve got good lighting  #glasstest #rash #meningitis #baby #toddler #infant #medicalemergency #doctor #paediatrics

Question 6 in my series of the 25 most googled health questions for children under the age of 5: When should I worry about a rash? Well firstly there are hundreds of different types of rashes that might occur in your little ones and it’s impossible to cover them all in one reel! However there is one test you can do to assess if your child has a particularly concerning rash called a “petechial” or “non-blanching” rash. This can be a sign of serious infections such as meningitis, clotting disorders or blood disorders…. The reason it does not go away when you press on it is that this rash is caused by bleeding from small blood vessels called capillaries in the skin - this blood will not fade when pressed on with a glass and that is why we call it a “non-blanching” rash.  If your child does have a non blanching rash don’t panic! ⚠️ There are other much less serious causes of non-blanching rashes including significant coughing or straining, viral illnesses such as flu or EBV or a pressure injury. My recommendation: assess the rash AND assess your child - are they otherwise unwell? Do they have any other signs of serious infection such as fever, lethargy, drowsiness, headache or neck pain? If you’re unsure at all get them checked out by a health professional. On darker skin this test may be more difficult to perform and the rash may be less visible so if your child has dark skin and a rash you are unsure about - please consult a health professional 👍🏻  If this is helpful please save this post for future reference. Remember this advice does not take the place of your registered healthcare practitioner. ☺️👍🏻  #rash #paediatrician #parenthood #mumlife #rashes #meningitis #sepsis #kidshealth #childhealth #a&edoctor #medicalstudents #healthadvice #toddlerlife #baby #newmum

On March 24th, I underwent surgery to remove a tumor from my pituitary gland on my brain stem, which had caused Cushing's Disease. I was expected to stay in the hospital for 4 days, but my stay ended up being 3 weeks due to meningitis, which led to 12 failed attempts at inserting canulas and ultimately required the insertion of a PICC line. I became extremely ill and felt as though I was dying. Now, 8 months later, I’m in remission, but I am adrenal insufficient and depend on replacement medication to stay alive. Meet my new little girl to help me on my journey to recovery.   This is Cookie, 9 weeks old Cavapoo.  She has already brought so many smiles, laughs and cuddles which is what I needed. I was told to bring family in who I would want to be with me to say goodbye. Saying goodbye to my daughters will forever break my heart.  I have a long road to recovery.  I am working with the surgical team, physio at home team to build me back up.
